cosy-lesson.title: Why Do We Try to Relate to ADHD?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Diagnose – identify the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

p.em: Example: Doctors often find it challenging to diagnose ADHD in adult patients correctly.

cosy-blockquote.p: Burnout – physical or mental collapse caused by overwork or stress.

p.em: Example: Many people mistake severe work-related burnout for an attention deficit disorder.

cosy-blockquote.p: Relate – feel sympathy for or identify with someone or something.

p.em: Example: It is natural to relate to social media posts that describe common struggles with focus.

cosy-blockquote.p: Neurodiversity – the range of differences in individual brain function and behavioral traits.

p.em: Example: Celebrating neurodiversity helps us understand that everyone's brain works differently.

cosy-blockquote.p: Symptom – a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease.

p.em: Example: Being easily distracted can be a symptom of ADHD, but it is also a very common human trait.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overestimate ≠ Underestimate – estimate something to be better or larger than it really is ≠ estimate something to be smaller or less important.

p.em: Example: We often overestimate our own attention span on good days, but underestimate how much fatigue affects our focus on bad ones.

cosy-blockquote.p: Label – a classifying phrase or name applied to a person or thing.

p.em: Example: Receiving a clinical label can sometimes bring a great sense of comfort and clarity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distraction – a thing that prevents someone from giving their full attention to something else.

p.em: Example: Smartphones provide a constant stream of distraction that ruins our productivity.
Example: A hyperactive mind can generate brilliant creative ideas but struggles to sit still.

cosy-blockquote.p: Empathy – the ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

p.em: Example: Learning about neurodiversity increases our empathy for coworkers who work in different ways.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why are we so highly anxious to adopt clinical labels for our routine struggles? Is it a convenient pretext to avoid personal accountability?
★ Have you ever blamed a bad day on your "temperament" solely to avoid apologizing for your behavior?

Is staying focused on a long book virtually impossible today, or do we merely lack the patience we used to have?
★ When was the last time you read a full page without reaching for your smartphone?

Why do we experience a creeping sense of apathy toward our actual responsibilities while feeling highly motivated by digital distractions?
★ How do you fight off a wave of professional apathy when your schedule is overloaded?

Is self-diagnosing on social media a stylized decoy, or is it an attempt to diagnose genuine pain in an un-empathetic world?
★ Have you ever used a minor physical symptom as a decoy to get out of an awkward social event?

Why has quiet, undistracted time become such an elusive luxury-is it precisely because we overestimate our multitasking ability while we underestimate our need for deep rest?
★ How do you create an elusive bubble of stillness in your daily routine?

Do we prioritize immediate sensory stimulation over deep, long-term goals simply because our brains have gotten used to instant rewards?
★ How do you decide which tasks to prioritize when your mind feels completely fragmented?

When someone claims they cannot focus on the pretext of "burnout", do you suspect they are merely bored or is their mind genuinely hyperactive?
★ Have you ever used the pretext of being exhausted just to escape an awkward conversation?

Does the constant scarcity of deep attention make our rare, focused conversations feel particularly precious, showing how much we hunger for genuine empathy?
★ Do you struggle with a sense of time scarcity even on your days off?

Do you reckon that digital technology has freed our hours, or has it simply fragmented our minds, making the concept of neurodiversity essential to understand our different attention spans?
★ Do you reckon you would be more creative in a slower, less connected era?

Can a clinical label act as a protective armor against the harsh, competitive demands of modern society?
★ What kind of mental armor do you wear when you feel you cannot meet people's expectations?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: - 🛡️A clinical label that explains your boundaries. (The Protective Armor) - 🔓A self-designed discipline without acronyms. (The Raw Autonomy)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Future societies will treat distraction as an environmental hazard rather than a personal cognitive failure.
★ Do you think we are highly addicted to the feeling of cognitive overload?

The term "ADHD" has become merely a trendy social decoy utilized by neurotypical adults to excuse poor planning.
★ Have you ever felt that trendy acronyms are simply oversimplifying deep, human dilemmas?

In a highly optimized world, achieving uninterrupted, quiet boredom will become the most elusive mental luxury.
★ Would you pay for a service that guarantees elusive, distraction-free time, or can you create it simply on your own?

To survive the upcoming attention crisis, future corporations must learn to prioritize slow, offline workflows over hyper-responsiveness.
★ Would you accept a lower salary if a company promised to prioritize your free time and mental peace?

True friendship cannot survive when encounters are scheduled weeks in advance on the pretext of professional efficiency.
★ Do you feel that scheduling a meet-up weeks in advance is merely a cold pretext, or is it a realistic necessity for adults?

Future generations will view our obsession with multitasking as a collective psychological disease rather than a career asset.
★ Do you think we are particularly addicted to the feeling of being busy because it makes us feel important?

Most futurists reckon that the smarter our devices become, the less patience we will have for slow, unstructured human interactions.
★ Do you reckon that instant digital replies have simply ruined our ability to enjoy a slow-paced relationship?

In our relentless pursuit of optimization, we are heading toward a future of complete sensory and emotional apathy where nothing makes our hearts beat faster.
★ How can we precisely combat the creeping apathy of modern life if we are always running after the next task?

Our ancestors viewed deep attention as a spiritual practice, whereas modern education has reduced it to a clinical commodity.
★ Have you ever experienced a state of "flow" where you forgot about time entirely?

A clinical label is the perfect armor for a modern adult who simply wants to say "I cannot do this anymore" to a demanding boss.
★ Have you ever wanted to say "no" but found yourself searching for a bulletproof excuse solely to be polite?
